summary: CCC-built Armintrout lookout, erected 1934 in Pike County, Ohio; moved and shortened to 60 ft in 2016; now at the ODNR park on the Ohio State Fairgrounds, not open to unassisted visits.

facts.design: Steel CCC-built fire lookout tower; metal legs re-galvanized, wooden landings and stairs replaced in 2016, cab refinished with new glass
facts.agency: Ohio Division of Forestry (NHLR administrator); displayed by the ODNR Natural Resources Park

staffing.status: Occupied by a lookout from October 1934; no end-of-watch date for this tower in the sources

access.note: Not open to unassisted public visits, per a 2016 Ohio's Country Journal article; not among the towers CompassOhio lists as open to climb. Current rules not confirmed; the ODNR tower page returned 404 in the cache.

visit.trail_note: Stands behind the Smokey Bear statue in the ODNR Natural Resources Park on the Ohio State Fairgrounds, Columbus. Check with ODNR before planning a visit.

events.note: Erected by CCC crews on Armintrout Road in Pike County; state paid $1 for a .35-acre site from the Armintrout family
Chillicothe Gazette item of Oct. 27, 1934 says the tower was being occupied by H. G. Armintrout
Ohio's lookout network ended; the panels say the last tower closed in 1978. This tower's own closing date is not given
Ownership transferred to the Pike County Public Service Trust for civil defense purposes
Dismantled, shortened to 60 ft (ground to bottom of cab), and re-erected at the ODNR Natural Resources Park on the Ohio State Fairgrounds
Legs sandblasted, acid dipped and re-galvanized; wooden landings and stairs replaced with state-forest wood; cab refinished with new glass

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The panels give the original height as 80 ft; Ohio's Country Journal gives 71 ft. Both say the tower is 60 ft tall now, measured to the bottom of the cab. The record uses 18.3 m (60 ft) for the current structure.

notes_for_editor: The ODNR tower page (ohiodnr.gov .../armintrout-fire-tower) returned 404 in the cache, and the current visiting rule rests on a 2016 article plus an undated CompassOhio guide, so access should be checked. Original height conflicts (80 ft in the panels, 71 ft in OCJ). The 1934 newspaper items spell the family name Armentrout; the NHLR and panels use Armintrout. The panels and OCJ describe the fairgrounds as the Ohio State Fairgrounds, not the Ohio Exposition Center named in the brief. No notable fire is named in any source read. The Weebly newspaper items come through a lookout-history site, not the newspaper itself.
